clue.text: Security wanting all to clear off

indicators.note: something off has gone wrong or is out of place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone guarding valuables complains that everything has been told to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the anagram of ALL TO CLEAR; 'wanting' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Collateral is property pledged as a guarantee for a loan, a form of financial security.

clue.text: Swimmer in quartet among 18 from the south

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the south means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards
a group of four letters is taken from among those of the referenced answer, its opening four

parts.note: the answer to 18 down is PRACTICAL

explanation.surface: A fish listed among a quartet of items in another clue, coming from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: The first four letters of PRACTICAL (18 down), PRAC, read upwards ('from the south') give CARP.
explanation.definitionFit: The carp is a freshwater fish, so a creature that swims.

clue.text: Ruined ancestral city

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the letters of the next word are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: An old family seat in a city has fallen into ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruined' signals the anagram of ANCESTRAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancaster is a historic city in north-west England, county town of Lancashire.

clue.text: Where one might find sportspeople are not available

explanation.surface: A team-sheet note that the athletes one expected to see are unavailable.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a stadium or venue where athletes compete.

clue.text: Timelessly seductive woman is queen

indicators.note: without time: both letters standing for time, the abbreviation T, are taken away

parts.note: a temptress is a woman who seduces

explanation.surface: An ageless femme fatale turns out to be royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the usual abbreviation for time; 'Timelessly' removes both Ts from TEMPTRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: An empress is a female sovereign, ranking as a queen does.

clue.text: Work in 'Bill & Ted' took over

indicators.note: the work piece is placed inside the pair formed by the bill and the name

parts.note: AD is short for advertisement, a bill or poster
the name is taken as it is
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A film like Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure was a hit and took over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill & Ted' reads as the film duo, but 'Bill' is an advert and 'Ted' simply a name, with the work going in between.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt an idea or cause is to take it over as one's own.

clue.text: Give up returning fashionable decadent clothes

indicators.note: returning means the hidden letters are read backwards
the phrase clothes the answer, wrapping its letters across the join of two words

explanation.surface: A fashion-conscious person abandons their old decadent wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' signals the hidden EDEC in 'fashionablE DECadent', and 'returning' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede territory or a point is to surrender it, handing it over.

clue.text: Perform in French before a court

parts.note: the French word for in is en

explanation.surface: An actor performs in French before a court audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact a role or scene is to act it out, to carry it through on stage.

clue.text: Just need van he'd damaged

indicators.note: damaged things are broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver says they simply need the van they have damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' signals the anagram of NEED VAN HE'D.
explanation.definitionFit: A just judge is fair and impartial, treating both sides equally.

clue.text: Look up Eastern wine — it enhances the memory

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to peek is to take a quick look
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: A tip to consult a guide to an oriental wine said to sharpen recall.
explanation.walkthrough: PEEK reversed by 'up' is KEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake is a memento, kept to remind you of a person or occasion.

clue.text: Compass moved quickly, finally pointing east

parts.note: to run is to move quickly; ran is its past tense

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A compass needle swung quickly and came to rest pointing east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compass' is not the instrument but scope or extent.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass in the sense of scope or extent matches range, as in the compass of a voice.

clue.text: Walk open-armed when upset

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A welcoming person storms off when upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when upset' signals the anagram of OPEN-ARMED.
explanation.definitionFit: A promenade is a leisurely stroll, and also a paved walkway along a seafront.

clue.text: Colourful creature, something in the garden to be eaten by cat?

indicators.note: the garden item is taken inside the animal, which swallows it

parts.note: a cat is an example of a pet
a rake is a tool found in a garden; 'something' gives the article a

explanation.surface: A bright bird in the garden is at risk of being eaten by the cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The cat is defined by example, hence the question mark: PET wraps A RAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Parakeets are small parrots with brightly coloured plumage.

clue.text: Plot way to catch cold

indicators.note: the path takes hold of the cold letter inside it

parts.note: a path is a way or track
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A scheme for avoiding a chill, or a garden plot where someone caught cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A patch is a small piece of ground, such as a vegetable plot.

clue.text: Story put out, very heartless and confused

indicators.note: letters put out of order are rearranged
heartless removes the central letters of the word

explanation.surface: A tale was released, extremely lacking in feeling and muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' cuts ER from VERY to leave VY; 'out' shuffles STORY + PUT + VY.
explanation.definitionFit: Topsy-turvy describes things upside down and in a state of muddle or disorder.

clue.text: Bans partner's parents after divorce?

definitions.meaning: to outlaw something is to forbid it
a jokey turn on in-laws: once the marriage is over they are out rather than in

explanation.surface: A rule forbidding contact with one's former in-laws after a split.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical, hence the question mark: in-laws become out-laws.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlaws as a verb means bans; as a joke noun it is the in-laws once divorce has happened.

clue.text: A crew competent and compliant

parts.note: a ship's crew are its men
able means capable or competent

explanation.surface: A ship's crew described as both capable and obedient.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amenable is willing to go along with requests, agreeable and cooperative.

clue.text: Expressionless corpse with power to drive medium away

indicators.note: the power letter comes in and pushes out the medium letter, replacing it
away confirms the medium letter leaves

parts.note: a dead man is a corpse
M is the abbreviation for medium, as on clothing labels
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A stony-faced spectre uses its power to banish a spiritualist medium.
explanation.walkthrough: P replaces M in DEAD MAN; 'medium' looks like a psychic but is the clothing-size letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan look or delivery shows no emotion, deliberately impassive.

clue.text: Realistic after rehearsal, shortened a line

indicators.note: shortened means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: practice is rehearsal

explanation.surface: After a rehearsal, an actor's speech was cut by one line to make it more believable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' only orders the surface; PRACTIC + A + L is in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical and realistic both describe a sensible, down-to-earth outlook.

clue.text: Hearts, perhaps, surrounding dodgy ref — it's too much

indicators.note: the suit wraps around the jumbled letters

parts.note: hearts is one example of a suit in cards

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fans are heartily sick of a crooked referee's decisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearts' is a card suit given by example, hence 'perhaps'; the jumbled referee goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an excess, more than is needed.

clue.text: Joint champions?

definitions.meaning: a cut of beef for roasting
the side at the top of a league are the winners; the question mark flags the playful split

explanation.surface: Asking whether shared winners are joint champions.
explanation.definitionFit: Topside is a lean roasting cut of beef, a joint; the side at the top of a league are its champions.

clue.text: Get into shape before couple's announcement

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: Getting fit before a couple announce their engagement.
explanation.walkthrough: PAIR said aloud gives PARE.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepare something is to get it ready, to put it into proper form.

clue.text: Swapping RE, senior pupil gets 10/10?

indicators.note: the two named letters change places in the word

parts.note: a prefect is a senior pupil given authority in a school

explanation.surface: A head pupil swapping to Religious Education scores full marks.
explanation.walkthrough: RE looks like Religious Education, a school subject, but is just the letters R and E to swap.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten out of ten is a flawless score, so the question mark signals an example of flawlessness.

clue.text: Article thanks Greek character

parts.note: the is the definite article
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A writer thanks a character from Greece for an article.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Professional leaving right and left boot out

indicators.note: the right letters leave, taken out of the word

parts.note: an expert is a professional

explanation.surface: A footballer who quits a club after kicking with both feet.
explanation.walkthrough: RT goes from EXPERT to give EXPE, then L for left.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel someone is to throw them out, as from a school.

clue.text: One hanging on where falling soldier might be found

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier who descends by parachute
a site is a place where something is found

explanation.surface: A parachutist dangling from a tree, and the spot where he would land.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite clings to a host, living off it, so it is one that hangs on.

clue.text: Cut mostly fine bundle

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: to shear is to cut, as with sheep
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Cutting most of something into a fine bundle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheaf is a bundle, such as of corn stalks or papers.

clue.text: Partner runs from part of tennis match

indicators.note: the runs letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: a rally is an exchange of shots in tennis
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A doubles player runs off court partway through a match.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a partner or associate in a shared cause.

clue.text: Super-vile, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals another arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Describing something as extremely vile, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals the anagram of SUPER-VILE, which also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extremely vile is revolting and disgusting in the highest degree.

clue.text: Better in extra large, as they say

indicators.note: what people say is spoken, so the letters are heard aloud

parts.note: XL is the clothing-size abbreviation for extra large

explanation.surface: A garment that looks better in a bigger size, according to people.
explanation.walkthrough: XL said aloud is ex-el, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to outdo or surpass others, so to better them.

clue.text: The old students shout

parts.note: ye is an old form of the
L is a learner, as on British driving L-plates; two give students

explanation.surface: Ancient students shouting.
explanation.definitionFit: A yell is a loud cry, a holler.

clue.text: Weaknesses shown by supporters of Cassius?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for a hidden flaw in an admired person
Cassius Clay, the boxer later Muhammad Ali, stood on his own two feet

explanation.surface: Pondering the frailties of the conspirator Cassius.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a hidden flaw in a revered figure, read literally as what the boxer Cassius Clay stood on.
